708165.t: From Proto-Hellenic *leukós, from Proto-Indo-European *lewk- (“white; light; bright”).

708196.t: Unknown. Has been compared to λεῖος (leîos, “smooth”), λιτός (lītós, “simple; plain”), Latin laedō (“to strike; to hurt”), Lithuanian slidùs (“slippery; slick”), Proto-Balto-Slavic *ledús (“ice”).

708171.t: Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀩𐀺 (re-wo /⁠léwōn⁠/). Many ancient languages possessed similar words for lion, including Akkadian 𒌨 (labbu) (reconstructed to Proto-Semitic *labiʾ-).

708151.t: From the stem of λέπω (lépō, “to peel”) + -ρός (-rós).

708149.t: Resembles λεπίς (lepís, “scale”) + *-ρα (*-rā), but with unclear morphology. Perhaps both words are ultimately Pre-Greek; compare λεβηρίς (lebērĭ́s, “shed skin”), and see λέπω (lépō, “to peel”) for more.

708147.t: Perhaps from λέπω (lépō, “to peel”) + -ις (-ĭs, feminine suffix).

708124.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *légō, from Proto-Indo-European *leǵ- (“to collect, gather”). Cognates include Latin legō and Albanian mbledh.

708140.t: From λέκος (lékos, “dish; pot; pan”) + -άνη (-ắnē, suffix for utensil names), alleged to be from Pre-Greek; however, see λάγυνος (lắgūnos, “flask”).

708139.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *leyǵʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-ti Proto-Indo-European *léyǵʰti Proto-Hellenic *léikʰō Ancient Greek λείχω From Proto-Indo-European *leyǵʰ-.

708135.t: From λειτουργός (leitourgós, “public servant”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun–forming suffix).

708175.t: From the Ancient Greek root λαβ- (lāb-), whence λαμβάνω (lambánō, “to take”), and -μα (-ma).

708156.t: Traditionally taken to be from an earlier *λέχ-σκα (*lékh-skā) with metathesis of the -σ- (-s-), a nominal formation from the same root as λέχομαι (lékhomai, “to recline”) and λέχος n (lékhos, “bed”).

708174.t: From Proto-Hellenic *lā́tʰā, from Proto-Indo-European *léh₂dʰeh₂, from *leh₂- (“to be concealed”) (whence λανθάνω (lanthánō)).

708108.t: From λατρεύς (latreús, “hired servant”) + -εύω (-eúō), the former from λάτρις (látris, “hired servant, handmaid”) + -εύς (-eús).

708173.t: Likely from the root of λαγαρός (lăgărós, “hollow; slack”).

708138.t: From λείχω (leíkhō, “to lick”), derived with the meaning “the one who licks”, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *leyǵʰ- (“to lick”).

708129.t: From an older form *λεῖϝος (*leîwos), itself from Proto-Indo-European *leh₁y-u- (“smooth”) and cognate to Latin lēvis (“smooth”).

708186.t: Borrowed from a Semitic language, probably from a Canaanite word cognate to Hebrew לְבוֹנָה (ləḇōnā, “frankincense”) and Arabic لُبَان (lubān, “frankincense”), from Proto-West Semitic *laban- (“white”).

708188.t: From a Semitic sound plural of the etymon of λίβανος (lĭ́bănos), which Beekes says derives from a Semitic root cognate to Hebrew לָבָן (“white”) and Arabic لَبَن (laban, “milk”).

708128.t: From λείπω (leípō, “to leave, to quit”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

708114.t: Probably of Pre-Greek origin, as suggested by the suffix -ανον. The denominative simplex λαχαίνω (lakhaínō, “to dig”), which has only late attestations, is probably a back-formation from compounded forms.

708177.t: From Proto-Hellenic *lāros, from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂- (expressive root). Cognate with Latin lātrō, Latin lamentum, λάλος (lálos), λάσκω (láskō).

708176.t: Unexplained. Perhaps a technical term of the Pre-Greek substrate.

708132.t: λειτουργός (leitourgós, “one who performs a λειτουργία, a public servant”) + -έω (-éō, denominative suffix).
